Yinyang appendices

Steal Fire, Then Become Fire

Join in the collective work of stealing fire, and use it to cultivate understanding, judgment, and creative capacity—to become someone who can keep generating.

Choose what to read and use

If literature, history, or philosophy is not your field, begin with relevant parts of Core views. Consider their reasons and conditions before adopting them, and follow the linked arguments when you want to go deeper. You need not read everything in order or accept every position.

Selected ideas can guide the configuration of a fitting personal environment. Work with a model to turn an understanding of your purposes, preferences, and circumstances into ways of cooperating, tools, and everyday arrangements. Using the Tools supplies an operational entrance.

Writing your own philosophy, essays, or website is a choice of interest. Begin by using the ideas to configure your environment if that serves you; explore Literary programming and related essays when you want to create. The five parts below present the author’s connected argument for selective reading.

Download the reading edition: 中文 PDF · English PDF

Use boundary: these philosophical ideas guide personal-environment configuration; they do not supply a method for revising psychological material. Yinyang must not be used for psychological self-help, self-diagnosis, mental-health assessment, or treatment. Full notice

01

Starting point: join in stealing fire, then use it to cultivate yourself

Preview the argument, establish value and agency, give cultivation its conditional rationale through super-cuteness, then embody that direction in Baby Heraclitus.

02

Understanding: retaining and exploring life trajectories

Shared work leaves versions, operations, conversations, and feedback. Connect them into a revisitable life trajectory, retaining questions, choices, grounds, and revisions as material for the next part’s shared reflection.

03

Encounter: shared reflection and mutual cultivation

Having worked together and left a trajectory, explore and reflect on this living material together, recognize each participant’s contribution, and cultivate relationships and capabilities through that encounter.

04

Formation: from personal philosophy to a form of practice

Write philosophy from trajectories and shared reflection; let speech and opposition develop understanding, distill personal models with living material, then realize a practice that can be sustained and revised.

05

Practice: continued testing and shared creation

Sustain the formed arrangement and examine its effects on life and capabilities. Offer useful works and methods to new encounters, whose trajectories can return to reflection and revisions of philosophy and models.

06

Yinyang appendices

Diagrams, core views, reading sources, and six writing guides accompany the arguments of stealing fire and Yinyang.
